name: Detroit Pistons
notes: The Pistons play in the NBA's Eastern Conference, Central Division, with home games at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit. After a franchise-record losing streak in 2023-24, the team rebounded sharply in 2024-25 under head coach J.B. Bickerstaff, returning to the playoffs behind a young core anchored by All-Star point guard Cade Cunningham and center Jalen Duren. The 2025-26 roster blends that young nucleus with added veteran depth (Duncan Robinson, Kevin Huerter, Gary Harris, John Collins) acquired via trade and free agency.

roster.facts: Franchise cornerstone who made First-Team All-NBA and finished fifth in 2025-26 MVP voting, now locked into a $269M max extension.
roster.name: Cade Cunningham

roster.facts: First-time All-Star and Third-Team All-NBA center in a tense contract standoff with Detroit, seeking $40M+ annually ahead of an October 1 deadline.
roster.name: Jalen Duren

roster.facts: Led the NBA in steals per game and earned All-Defensive First Team honors in 2025-26, with a roughly $162M extension reportedly in the works.
roster.name: Ausar Thompson

roster.facts: Detroit's marquee offseason addition at power forward via a six-team trade, bringing 13.6 points and 55% shooting into the new starting five.
roster.name: John Collins

roster.facts: Arrived via sign-and-trade from Miami on a 3-year, $48M deal to be Detroit's marquee floor-spacer alongside Cade Cunningham.
roster.name: Duncan Robinson

roster.facts: Acquired at the February 2026 trade deadline while Detroit led the East at 36-12, then re-signed for $27M to keep the shooting intact.
roster.name: Kevin Huerter

roster.facts: Traded in from Oklahoma City this offseason after a career-high 11.1 points and 42.3% from three, adding elite bench shooting to Detroit's rotation.
roster.name: Isaiah Joe

roster.facts: First-round pick Detroit traded up for in the 2026 draft, an All-ACC scorer out of Stanford who lit up Summer League at nearly 20 a night.
roster.name: Ebuka Okorie

roster.facts: Veteran 3-and-D wing added in a July 2026 trade from Milwaukee, expected to be a rotation contributor heading into his age-33 season.
roster.name: Taurean Prince

roster.facts: Came over in the same Milwaukee trade as Prince, but injury history and a crowded wing rotation likely push him to deep-reserve minutes.
roster.name: Gary Harris

roster.facts: 2025 second-round pick out of Tennessee who was quiet as a rookie but exploded for 17.4 points a game in the 2026 Summer League.
roster.name: Chaz Lanier

roster.facts: The 2024 No. 5 overall pick enters year three still chasing a breakout role after a disappointing sophomore season on the wing.
roster.name: Ronald Holland II

roster.facts: Detroit's third big and injury insurance, with his $5.6M salary for 2026-27 fully guaranteed by the team on September 2, 2026.
roster.name: Paul Reed

roster.facts: Re-signed for one more year at $3.95M after playing all 82 games in 2025-26 as Detroit's reliable energy-off-the-bench veteran.
roster.name: Javonte Green

roster.facts: Undrafted free-agent success story who parlayed two-way minutes into an $8M deal after starting seven games and shooting 39% from three.
roster.name: Daniss Jenkins

roster.facts: Converted from a two-way deal to a standard contract in April 2026, now Detroit's third-string center depth behind Duren and Reed.
roster.name: Tolu Smith

roster.facts: Fringe two-way piece who saw just six games in 2025-26 and has reportedly flirted with a move to EuroLeague's KK Partizan.
roster.name: Wendell Moore Jr.
